subject_entity.notes: Arian church historian Philostorgius's 12-book history (c. 425) covering 300–425; survives mostly in Photius's epitome; key source for Theophilus the Indian's mission to Himyar (3.4–6) and Constantius II's religious diplomacy.

object_entity.notes: Arian church historian; wrote a 12-book Ecclesiastical History (c. 425) covering 300–425; survives mostly in Photius's epitome; key source for Theophilus the Indian's mission and Constantius II's religious diplomacy.

evidence.notes: HE 3.4 is from Philostorgius's own work.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Theophilus called the Indian was sent by Emperor Constantius on an embassy to the Himyarites in south Arabia. He was originally from the island of Dibus (Socotra). He converted the Himyarites and built three churches: one in Zafar the capital, one in Aden, and one near the Persian Gulf. He also visited the Aksumites and corrected their worship.
passage.notes: Key source for Arabian/Himyarite Christianity and Theophilus's mission; preserved in Photius's epitome.

object_entity.notes: Systematic persecution of Christians in the Sasanian Empire beginning c. 340 under Shapur II; motivated partly by Constantine's declaration of Rome as a Christian empire; Aphrahat wrote his later Demonstrations during this crisis; lasted intermittently until Shapur's death in 379.
